label: object pronouns
note: Closed by chapters 260-262. The six independent first- and second-person accusatives are taught one number at a time: mām/tvām, āvām/yuvām, then asmān/yuṣmān. A separate rule lesson makes the learner choose person and number, and a terminal retrieval produces all six in the already-known paśyati frame. This is deliberately not a claim that the first two personal-pronoun paradigms are complete: their short enclitic alternatives, respectful bhavantam and third-person objects remain outside this point.
